title: Development Program Manager (Q-Systems: Connectivity)
location_raw: Ashburn, VA; Richmond, VA; Piscataway, NJ; New Albany, OH; Salem, PA
description:
Who we are:
As a global leader in digital infrastructure, QTS designs, builds and operates advanced data centers that support strategic AI, cloud and digital transformation initiatives. We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be.

Who we are:
It's pretty exciting to find yourself standing in a pivotal moment in time. It’s even more exciting to be out front leading it. At QTS, our world-class data centers are supporting our customers’ most strategic growth initiatives, positioning us at the forefront of today’s dynamic digital transformation.

As AI and cloud drive the demand for increased speed, capacity and capability, QTS has emerged as the global digital infrastructure leader, committed to connecting the world for good. Driven by purpose and fueled by a spirit of innovation, QTS designs, builds and operates some of the world’s most advanced, forward-thinking data centers. QTS is a portfolio company of Blackstone.

QTS is Powered by People. People who play a vital role in our company’s culture, innovation and growth. People who are committed to contributing to the communities where we operate and work. People who are knowledgeable, resourceful and mission driven. Together, we do great things.

Who You Are:
The Development Program Manager (Q-Systems: Connectivity) is primarily responsible for leading and managing Q-Systems (with a focus on telecom and networking) for design, pre-construction and construction activities across several campuses. The Program Manager will interact daily with Facilities, Contractors, Designers, Engineers, Commissioning Agents, Vendors, and Data Center Operations staff and should have both written and oral communication skills commensurate with this level of regular communication.

The Impact You Will Have:
Q-Systems is a technology team within the QTS Development organization. Q-Systems ensures critical facility operation systems are designed and implemented per our basis of design documents to ensure our buildings operate per requirements. The critical facility operation systems include the QTS corporate network, facility network, wireless access points, BMS / EPMS control systems and security technology. Each of these systems ride on the QTS low voltage network. Deployment of the network infrastructure is a key component to ensure projects are complete per tenant lease and project construction schedules.

What You Will Do:

- The Development Program Manager (Q-Systems: Connectivity) is primarily responsible for leading and managing the design, pre-construction and construction activities on a given project. The Project Manager will interact on a daily basis with Facilities, Contractors, Designers, Engineers, Commissioning Agents, Vendors, and Data Center Operations staff and should have both written and oral communication skills commensurate with this level of regular communication

- Program level support for network infrastructure deployments across our portfolio

- Coordinate with QTS network infrastructure and technology teams to ensure infrastructure meets the facility needs

- Support our Q-Systems team with network infrastructure coordination

- Manage port schedule creation for development projects

- Review project design to ensure compliance with QTS system standards and Basis of Design documents.

- Create and communicate updates on development program & project status suitable for executive level reviews. Effectively present information in a manner to support efficient decision making

- Implement and manage multi-phased site development plans to achieve time, budget, and quality standards in a predictable fashion. Continuously update a campus master plan to provide predictable statistics in a dynamic environment

- Write scopes of work for design, construction, commissioning services & participate in procurement and project cost estimates

- Evaluate and level pricing proposals for design, construction, and commissioning services

- Establish project schedules and manage teams to on-time completion

- Develop plans for product deployment and review/communicate plans with QTS staff involved

- Establish and maintain relationships serving as liaison with key QTS stakeholders

- Represent QTS Q-Systems interests as leader in OAC and low voltage meetings

- Review project implementations to ensure compliance with approved design documents, QTS system standards and Basis of Design documents.

- Create & build relationships that enhance QTS's ability to be a leader in creating the World's Most Valuable Data Center Real Estate

- Work with the internal development team to enhance project management processes and protocols

- Develop relationship with QTS Facility Operations Technology teams to understand their needs and deliver technologies that support facility operations needs

What You Will Need to be Successful (basic qualifications):

- Bachelor’s degree in Technology, Engineering or Construction Management field or equivalent professional experience

- 8-10+ years of experience with delivery of mission critical data center facilities

- 8-10+ years of experience with management of technology design, implementation and project management.

- Experience with Microsoft Office suite, specifically PowerPoint for use in communicating program updates to executive-level and Excel to create and maintain site program & individual project budgets

- US Citizenship for this position is required by law due to federal customer contracts

- Be able to travel up to 50% of the time. Average travel anticipated to be every other week for 2-3 days.

Other Key Skills:

- Experience designing technology systems for data centers, critical medical, industrial, construction, oil and gas, or large-scale technology systems.

- Project Management or Project Lead experience in large-scale projects.

- Experience in the construction of data centers, critical medical, industrial, construction, oil and gas, or large-scale technology systems.

- Strong knowledge of technology industry standards, procedures, and methodologies

- Advance knowledge of technology systems and their integration into mission-critical environments.

- Basic multidisciplinary knowledge of mission critical systems, design process, pre-construction requirements, and the construction process.

- Proven ability to communicate complex technical issues to leadership or non-engineers.

- Manage design consultants and technology trades

- Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with all levels of the organization

- Must be a capable, proven team player that both fosters and operates well within internal and external team environments.

- Able to solve problems at a tactical and functional level

- Strong Verbal and Written Communication Skills

- Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

The Perks (and these are just a few!):

- Q-Rest Sabbatical

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan

- QTS scholarship for dependents

- Eagle Club Award Trip Eligibility

- Paid Volunteer and Floating days

- Tuition Assistance, Parental Leave and Military Leave Assistance

title: Development Project Engineer – Fire Protection & Fire Alarm
location_raw: Ashburn, VA; York, SC; Duluth, GA; Irving, TX; Atlanta, GA
description:
Who we are:
As a global leader in digital infrastructure, QTS designs, builds and operates advanced data centers that support strategic AI, cloud and digital transformation initiatives. We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be.

The Development Project Engineer – Fire Protection & Fire Alarm is primarily responsible for assisting with the design, preconstruction, procurement, construction, testing, and commissioning activities for fire protection, fire alarm, and life safety systems across assigned projects. The Project Engineer will interact daily with Facilities, Contractors, Designers, Engineers, Commissioning Agents, Vendors, Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), Insurance Representatives, and Data Center Operations staff and should possess written and verbal communication skills commensurate with this level of engagement.
KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

- Review drawing packages for adherence to fire protection, fire alarm, and life safety design standards.

- Collaborate with internal and external design teams to evaluate designs to ensure compliance with established design standards, local code requirements, insurance requirements, and AHJ requirements.

- Partner with internal and external stakeholders to define project scope requirements, evaluate deviations from standards, and communicate requirements to design teams.

- Work with construction, commissioning, and risk management teams to answer Requests for Information (RFIs), code interpretations, and value engineering proposals.

- Collaborate with the procurement team to review OFCI equipment submittals for compliance with fire protection and fire alarm design criteria.

- Support project teams in resolving fire protection and fire alarm design issues discovered during construction, testing, and commissioning phases.

- Work closely with strategic procurement teams on fire protection and fire alarm equipment procurement.

- Assist in reviewing fire protection hydraulic calculations, fire pump analyses, water supply evaluations, and system acceptance testing requirements.

- Assist in reviewing fire alarm system architectures, battery calculations, sequence of operations, cause-and-effect matrices, and integrated testing plans.

- Support factory witness testing, site acceptance testing, integrated systems testing, and commissioning activities.

- Coordinate with AHJs, insurance representatives, consultants, contractors, and commissioning teams to support project approvals and occupancy milestones.

- Support development and maintenance of standardized fire protection and fire alarm design standards for mission-critical facilities.

- Assist with evaluating fire suppression, fire detection, emergency communications, and life safety systems for compliance and operational reliability.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Construction Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience.

- Basic experience with fire protection, fire alarm, life safety, construction, commissioning, facility operations, or engineering design.

- Familiarity with engineering drawings, specifications, submittals, and construction documents.

- Understanding of fire suppression systems, fire alarm systems, smoke detection systems, and life safety systems.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience designing, supporting, or reviewing fire protection and fire alarm systems for data centers, mission-critical facilities, industrial facilities, or large commercial developments.

- Assist with project management responsibilities across multiple projects and campuses.

- Experience with fire alarm sequence of operations, cause-and-effect matrices, system testing, and commissioning activities.

- Direct experience in the construction of data centers, critical medical facilities, industrial facilities, or other mission-critical environments.

- Basic knowledge of NFPA standards, including but not limited to NFPA 13, NFPA 20, NFPA 24, NFPA 72, NFPA 75, NFPA 76, NFPA 101, and NFPA 4, as well as applicable building and fire codes.

- Familiarity with FM Global Data Sheets, insurance requirements, and loss prevention strategies.

- Experience with double-interlock pre-action sprinkler systems, clean agent systems, water-based suppression systems, and special hazard protection systems.

- Experience with VESDA and aspirating smoke detection systems, very early warning fire detection systems, and integration with monitoring and control platforms.

- Experience supporting integrated systems testing, acceptance testing, and commissioning of fire protection and life safety systems.

- Experience evaluating performance-based fire protection alternatives and alternative means and methods.

- Basic knowledge of fire protection, fire alarm, and life safety systems and their integration into mission-critical environments.

- Basic multidisciplinary knowledge of electrical, mechanical, controls, commissioning, pre-construction requirements, and construction processes.

- Ability to communicate technical issues to senior leadership, consultants, contractors, AHJs, insurers, and non-technical stakeholders.

- NICET certification, EIT certification, CFPS certification, or a desire to pursue industry certifications is preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

- Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to interface with all levels of the organization.

- Must be a capable, proven team player who fosters and operates effectively within internal and external team environments.

- Ability to solve problems at a tactical and functional level.

- Strong verbal and written communication skills.

- Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

- Strong understanding of fire protection, fire alarm, life safety, and regulatory compliance requirements.

- Ability to review, interpret, and communicate engineering drawings, specifications, calculations, and testing requirements.

- Understanding of risk management principles and fire protection strategies for mission-critical facilities.

- Ability to balance code compliance, operational reliability, maintainability, and project requirements when evaluating technical solutions.

QTS-Specific Preferred Experience

- Experience supporting hyperscale and colocation data center developments.

- Familiarity with FM-insured facilities, critical environment risk mitigation, and integrated testing of fire protection systems supporting Tier III and Tier IV mission-critical infrastructure.

- Experience working with owners, contractors, consultants, and commissioning teams in fast-paced data center development environments.

title: Manager, Facilities Operations Engineer
location_raw: Cedar Rapids, IA; New Albany, OH; Chicago, IL
description:
The Manager of Facilities Operations Engineering will be responsible for the Data Center facility technical strategy, continuous improvement and development support for sites across the QTS portfolio. This role is ultimately responsible to assist with the engineering related to coordination, installation, and integration aspects of electrical and mechanical systems, operations, and maintenance for critical and non-critical electrical & mechanical systems alike within the QTS portfolio. This role requires keen planning skills along with the ability to lead through influence and to be a proactive partner with a strong engineering orientation. The ideal candidate will have experience in electrical and/or mechanical systems and possess knowledge of large-scale data centers (or similar environments). These environments may include state-of-the-art electrical distribution systems, static UPS, emergency standby generation, fire alarm/suppression, monitoring systems, as well as chiller and large-scale cooling systems. This role will be a platform role that will require an estimated 10-30% travel to other sites around the U.S.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES - Other duties may be assigned.
· Provide technical support to all aspects of data center operations including the operation, maintenance and repair of all mission critical equipment and systems supporting a 24x7 data center operation to achieve 100% uptime and 100% compliance with all customer SLAs.
· Provide Operations input for QTS standards and infrastructure solutions (in conjunction with other QTS departments).
· Assist in all site construction activity and installations, in coordination with QTS project departments, external construction resources, to ensure system design, installation and testing adhere to operational standards. Witness testing of all equipment during commissioning and validate sequence of operations and receipt of all operational documentation.
· Support for customer solutions, in coordination with Sales Engineering, Design & Construction and Colocation Operations to coordinate technical solutions and drawings for customer move-ins and turn-ups, including deployments and power circuit installations.
· Implement standard procedures and provide technical support for all sites for continuous improvement and root-cause problem solving efforts.
· Assist site engineering/management with compliance with local health & safety (i.e. OSHA) standards and national electrical and building codes.
· Interfaces with vendors, QTS Engineering, QTS Development and peer operations organizations.
· Coordinate and work with all QTS site teams on standard operating procedures (SOP), method of procedures (MOP), and emergency response procedures (ERP) established for the critical environments, as well as the formal change management process.
· Responsible for program management and oversight for execution of preventive maintenance and reporting for all sites.
· Provide coaching, mentoring and technical support to Critical Environment Engineers.

· Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering or similar HVAC or critical power certifications OR equivalent professional experience in lieu of degree
· Three or more years of direct experience with engineering related activities in a technical or critical environment (data center, nuclear power, hospital, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial/commercial field engineering)

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
· Five or more years of direct experience with engineering related activities in a technical or critical environment (data center, nuclear power, hospital, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial/commercial field engineering)
· Three or more years of data center specific experience.
· Two or more years of management/supervisory experience overseeing engineering or critical operations managers.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES
· Must be fluent with and possess an excellent working knowledge of Data Center Critical Environments
· Ability to develop solutions and create technical strategic and tactical plans on complex projects
· Ability and willingness to think outside of the box to find creative and innovative solutions to improve quality / reliability and continuously drive down operating costs
· Advanced understanding of both mechanical and electrical equipment, systems and design related to data centers. (Including but not limited to: uninterruptable power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers (air-cooled and water-cooled), pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers.)
· Extensive knowledge of electricity and medium / low voltage electrical distribution systems.
· Extensive experience with emergency backup systems (generators, UPS, battery backup).
· Knowledge and experience with preventative maintenance and work order software systems.

TOTAL REWARDS
This role is also eligible for a competitive beneﬁts package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; ﬂexible spending and HSA accounts; paid holidays; paid time off; paid volunteer days; employee assistance program; tuition assistance; parental leave; military leave assistance; QTS scholarship for dependents; wellness program, and other company beneﬁts. The Director, Development (Data Center Construction) requires strong interpersonal, communication and organizational skills, ability to self-direct, strong background in data center design, engineering, controls, and operational requirements, with an emphasis on project/construction management. In this role, you will function as QTS’ point of contact for new client builds and implementations and liaise between the QTS Sales Team (Account Exec and Sales Engineer), the QTS Operations Team, the QTS Property Development Team, and the Customer. The PSCM will work closely with existing Development Construction Project Managers to ensure the customers’ needs are carried out to high levels of expectation.

The position will report into the QTS Property Development department and work closely with the CHO and CRO, depending on the origin of the project.

What You Will Do:

- Manage the customer deployment project delivery for each sold deal within each QTS location

- Coordinate with the QTS Property Development team, and supporting specialty consultants, to support customer’s design needs, pricing, customer approvals, & implementation of specific deployment scopes

- Manage the delivery of these projects, this position aligns clients’ objectives, business processes, vendor management strategies, and cross-group collaboration efforts across the QTS organization

- Drive effective client relationship management and efficient cost management, with the ultimate goal of delivering the project on time and on budget

- Serve as a single contact for Federal sales support on potential secured deals

What You Will Need to be Successful (basic qualifications):

- Bachelor’s Degree and/or professional licenses in Construction Management or Electrical/Mechanical Engineering or Architecture

- Ten or more years of progressive responsibility in development of Mission Critical Facilities

- Five or more years of responsibility of data center project construction with large-scale data centers or DC lease providers

- Be able to travel as needed for the business.

Other Key Skills:

- Experience managing multiple large, multi-faceted projects

- Experience with Construction Health & Safety Knowledge

- Experience with Customer Deployment Technologies and Equipment, RCDD a plus.

- Strong Verbal and Written Communication Skills

- Ability to independently manage deadlines and support staff

- Ability to influence cross-discipline teams

- Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing situations at a high growth company

This role will oversee, document, and track various aspects of commissioning activities. Activities will include but are not limited to testing and/or validation of connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, transformers, electrical switchgear, UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply), STS (Static Transfer Switch), PDU (Power Distribution Unit), electrical distribution equipment, Chillers, water loops/components, Cooling distribution equipment, Electrical Power Monitoring Systems, and Building Management and automation systems. This role will also serve as a project manager and liaison to a third-party commissioning agent. This role requires work hours to support construction/commissioning activities of data center environments, which may include nights and/or weekends.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Develop and test site specific standard operating procedures (SOP), method of procedures (MOP), and emergency response procedures (ERP) in coordination with facilities operations.

title: Manager, Document Control
location_raw: Atlanta, GA; Richmond, VA
description:
Who we are:
As a global leader in digital infrastructure, QTS designs, builds and operates advanced data centers that support strategic AI, cloud and digital transformation initiatives. We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be.
Owns the Facilities Capital document control strategy, standards, and systems for QTS   as the owner   across the project   lifecycle, and   leads the team that executes it. The role governs two disciplines end to end: (1) design-document control —   defining QTS documentation requirements   and   verifying that   Architects, Engineers, OFCI vendors, and Contractors   deliver, review, and revise drawings, submittals, and RFIs to those requirements with a complete, defensible audit trail ; and (2) closeout/ turnover documentation — defining acceptance criteria for   as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties,   permits, and asset data, then reviewing, accepting, and transmitting the record set   to Technical Operations at   Substantial and Final Completion. Embeds document control requirements into A/E and contractor agreements, enforces compliance through project governance and closeout milestones, and safeguards the confidentiality and retention of critical infrastructure records.   As a people leader, sets document control policy, manages and develops the Document Control Lead, and represents document control in project governance. Reports to the Sr. Manager, Project Controls and partners closely with the Manager, Data Analytics & Information Management so controlled records feed the governed CPR data foundation and remain  audit-ready .

What You Will Do :  ( Job Responsibilities)

Design Documentation Control (Primary Focus)

- Establish and govern the enterprise document and information control system that all CPR projects operate within, defining QTS numbering, naming, revision, and metadata standards and confirming each project is set up to them.

- Maintain   the owner’s record   of all drawings and design documents issued by   the design team (A/E)   and Contractors through each project stage, with   revision and   status   verified against the contract deliverable list .

- Govern the owner’s RFI, submittal, and design-review workflows — consolidating QTS comments, meeting contractual review windows, verifying teams are working from the current Issued-for-Construction set, and escalating overdue or at-risk items to the Project Team.

- Define QTS   BIM , model,   and   data deliverable requirements   (e.g., Autodesk ACC / BIM 360 ),   verify   delivered   models   and   drawing registers   meet them , and resolve issues that threaten information flow or audit-trail integrity .

- Draft and maintain the document control, as-built, and turnover requirement exhibits used in QTS RFPs and A/E, contractor, and vendor agreements, so documentation obligations are contractually enforceable from award.

- Control access to sensitive site, security, and critical-infrastructure drawings — administering permissions, watermarking, and controlled-distribution rules for internal staff and external partners.

Closeout & Handover Documentation (Primary Focus)

- Own turnover documentation requirements and acceptance criteria — as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, permits, and asset data — defining what constitutes an acceptable record set, formally accepting or rejecting submissions from the design team and contractors, and transmitting the approved record set to Technical Operations at Substantial and Final Completion.

- Enforce delivery of turnover documentation through contract terms and project governance, recommending retention or closeout milestone holds where submissions are incomplete or non-compliant.

- Partner with Technical Operations to define and verify the asset, equipment, and warranty data required at turnover, ensuring it is delivered in a structured format that loads cleanly into the CMMS / asset management system.

- Administer records retention, legal hold, audit support, and long-term archiving of capital project documentation — including permits, inspection records, AHJ correspondence, and contract documents — producing records on request for audit, insurance, or claims and disputes.

- Establish Day-2 / Facilities Capital document control discipline   and   capture   lessons learned at each project stage   into   the CPR lessons-learned repository.

Standards, Governance & Team Leadership

- Author and maintain document control guidance, procedures, and administrative standards aligned to QTS protocols — serving as the subject-matter expert for design and closeout documentation across the CPR portfolio.

- Manage, develop, and set priorities for the Document Control Lead, and provide   functional   direction and   training   to Project Administrators,   design firms , and contractors on QTS document control standards .

- Govern user access and permissions across QTS document control platforms, and audit design team and contractor compliance with contractual documentation requirements — driving continuous improvement in standards and project set-up.

- Represent document control in project governance and gate reviews, reporting documentation compliance and turnover-readiness KPIs into the project reporting cycle.

Systems & Integration

- Administer and maintain Autodesk Construction Cloud / Forma as the QTS platform of record for project management and document control — owning project set-up, folder and permission structures, naming and revision standards, workflow configuration, and template governance across the CPR portfolio.

description:

title: Director, Facilities Operations Commissioning
location_raw: Richmond, VA; Ashburn, VA; Atlanta, GA; Manassas, VA
description:
The Director, Facilities Engineering Commissioning will be responsible for overseeing the technical strategy for commissioning, continuous improvement, and developmental support for sites throughout the QTS portfolio. This role will provide oversight and assistance with commissioning-related engineering, including the coordination, installation, and integration of connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, transformers, electrical switchgear, UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply), STS (Static Transfer Switch), PDU (Power Distribution Unit), electrical distribution equipment, Chillers, water loops/components, Cooling distribution equipment, Electrical Power Monitoring Systems, and Building Management and automation systems, within the QTS portfolio. The position demands strong planning abilities coupled with leadership through influence and a proactive partnership approach, underpinned by a robust engineering background. The ideal candidate will bring experience in electrical and mechanical systems, along with an understanding of large-scale data centers (or comparable environments), which may encompass cutting-edge electrical distribution systems, static UPS, emergency standby generation, fire alarm/suppression, monitoring systems, and extensive cooling systems.

This role will be a platform role that will require an estimated 10-30% travel to other sites around the U.S.
RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Manage the commissioning team, develop capabilities, engage employees, and set policies necessary to satisfy proper testing and turnover from development business partners.

- Implement operating and commissioning standards required for quality, safety, and ongoing operation.

- Manage expenditures and staffing to ensure compliance with financial goals. Oversee operational budgets to ensure compliance with organizational expenditure requirements.

- Assist in all site construction activity and installations, in coordination with QTS project departments, external construction resources, to ensure system design, installation and testing adhere to operational standards. Witness testing of all equipment during commissioning and validate sequence of operations and receipt of all operational documentation.

- Drive innovation into facilities programs/systems with an environmentally conscious attitude.

- Interfaces with vendors, QTS Engineering, QTS Development and peer operations organizations.

title: Commissioning Engineer II (Mechanical)
location_raw: Eagle Mountain, UT; Salt Lake City, UT; US UT Remote; Spanish Fork, UT
description:
The Commissioning Engineer II is responsible for but not limited to Level 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 commissioning of base building systems, security systems, life safety systems, Electrical, Mechanical, and EPMS/BMS systems of a Data Center environment.  This role will oversee, document, and track various aspects of commissioning activities.  Activities will include but are not limited to testing and/or validation of connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, transformers, electrical switchgear, UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply), STS (Static Transfer Switch), PDU (Power Distribution Unit), electrical distribution equipment, Chillers, water loops/components, Cooling distribution equipment, Electrical Power Monitoring Systems, and Building Management and automation systems.  This role will also serve as a project manager and liaison to a third-party commissioning agent.  This role requires work hours to support construction/commissioning activities of data center environments, which may include nights and/or weekends.
This role will be a platform role that may require an estimated 75% travel to other sites around the U.S.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Assist in all site construction activity and installations, in coordination with QTS Development Team, external construction resources, to ensure system design, installation and testing adhere to operational standards.

- Develop comprehensive commissioning plans for Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, and Level 5 systems, including connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, Electrical, Mechanical, and Building Automation components.

- Conduct thorough commissioning activities, ensuring that all systems are installed, tested, and validated according to industry standards and client specifications.

- Identify, track, and resolve any issues during the commissioning process, working closely with the project team to resolve technical challenges.  Utilize findings and provide feedback to program management team to drive continuous improvement.

- Create and/or review detailed commissioning documentation, including test procedures, reports, and as-built documentation, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

- Witness testing of all equipment during commissioning and validate sequence of operations and receipt of all operational documentation.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design engineers, project managers, contractors, commissioning agents, and facilities operations to ensure seamless integration of systems during the commissioning phase without impact to operational portions of the campus or building.

- Implement quality control measures to ensure the highest standards are met during the build and commissioning process, adhering to regulatory requirements and industry best practices.

- Develop and test site specific standard operating procedures (SOP), method of procedures (MOP), and emergency response procedures (ERP) in coordination with facilities operations.

- Provide training to end-users and maintenance personnel on the operation and maintenance of commissioned systems.

- Uses the Change Management Process to get approval for preventative and corrective maintenance.  Commences & completes the maintenance along with the necessary documentation using the QTS process and software.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Project Management, Computer Science, or a related field or equivalent professional experience

- Five or more years of work experience in data center engineering, commissioning, project management, or equivalent.

- Background in areas of building maintenance, CCTV and Access control systems, network, telecommunications, and/or fire detection/suppression systems.

- Ability to travel to other Data Center locations as required.

- Proficiency with MS Office Suite.

- US Citizenship for this position is required by law due to federal customer contracts

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Firm understanding of both mechanical and electrical equipment, systems and design related to data centers.

- Knowledge of electricity and medium to low voltage electrical distribution systems

- Experience with emergency backup systems (generators, UPS, battery backup)

- Knowledge of equipment operation and maintenance, single line drawings, critical scripted work, and sequence of operations.

- The ability to acquire and apply job-related knowledge within set guidelines and expectations.

- Ability to develop solutions and create technical plans on projects
- Strong written, verbal and interpersonal skills.

title: Global Process Owner - Capacity Strategy & Planning
location_raw: Atlanta, GA; Irving, TX; Overland Park, KS
description:
Who You Are: (Job Summary)
The Global Process Owner (GPO), Integrated Business Planning (IBP) is accountable for the design, standardization, governance, and integrity of the IBP process across QTS. This role ensures IBP is executed consistently, predictably, and with appropriate controls across all functions, regions, and planning horizons.
The IBP GPO operates within the enterprise GPO operating model, partnering closely with the IBP Director or Senior Director (who owns the IBP management system, executive cadence, and outcomes) and the GPO Leader (who governs enterprise‑wide process standards and consistency). The IBP GPO does not own business results or executive decision forums; instead, this role ensures the process, data, controls, and standards underlying IBP are decision‑grade and scalable.

What You Will Do: (Job Responsibilities)
Initial Focus Area: Capacity Strategy & Planning

- The Capacity Strategy & Planning Global Process Owner is accountable for the end-to-end process es associated with where and when QTS invests (market strategy, site selection, utilities, connectivity and portfolio forecasting). This role’s process scope includes:

- Opportunity identification

- Capital planning alignment

- Capacity pl anning and infrastructure readiness

- Site selection & due diligence

- Utility/power feasibility

- Connectivity

- Handoff to capital delivery/project development teams

IBP Process Ownership & Governance

- Own end‑to‑end accountability for the IBP process domain, including process boundaries, decision points, controls, and escalation paths across demand, supply, financial, capital, and capacity planning.

- Define and maintain the IBP process taxonomy (L1–L5), including standardized definitions, ownership, handoffs, and documentation aligned with enterprise process standards.

- Establish and enforce IBP process governance, including planning stage gates, reconciliation rules, approval frameworks, and exception handling.

- Manage intake, prioritization, and sequencing of IBP process changes, assessing enterprise impacts, risk, and control implications.

- Ensure IBP process governance aligns with enterprise initiative and process governance frameworks.

Standards, Controls & Data Integrity

- Develop and maintain standardized IBP artifacts, including process maps, SOPs, calendars, RACIs, control points, and KPI definitions.

- Define and govern critical IBP data elements and assumptions, including ownership, lineage, validation rules, and data quality thresholds.

- Partner with systems and data teams to translate IBP process standards into system requirements and embedded controls.

- Apply and evolve the GPO Playbook to ensure consistent documentation depth, governance rigor, and audit readiness.

Performance Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

- Define and maintain IBP process KPIs focused on planning effectiveness, timeliness, compliance, and decision readiness.

- Maintain transparent dashboards highlighting performance, variation, and exceptions across the IBP cycle.

- Use analytics and process insights to identify bottlenecks, control gaps, and improvement opportunities.

- Drive prioritized process improvements that strengthen consistency, comparability, and scalability.

Enablement & Adoption

- Support adoption of IBP standards through training guidance, communications, readiness criteria, and compliance reinforcement.

- Coordinate rollout of IBP process changes with the IBP Director / Senior Director and enterprise change partners.

- Reinforce disciplined planning behaviors and adherence to enterprise standards.

Scope and Impact

- Enterprise‑wide ownership of IBP process standards and controls

- Regular interaction with senior functional leaders and process councils

- Direct influence on planning consistency, data integrity, and decision quality

- Other duties as assigned.

What You Will Need to Be Successful:   (Required Qualifications, Education, Experience, Certifications)

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

- 7+ years of experience in IBP, S&OP, enterprise planning, or global process ownership.

- Demonstrated success establishing governance, standards, controls, and KPIs in complex environments.

- Strong influence skills in matrixed organizations without direct authority.

Nice to Have: (Preferred Qualifications, Education, Experience, Certifications)

- Advanced degree and certifications (Lean Six Sigma, PMP) a plus.

- Experience with process analytics or process mining platforms preferred.

title: Director, Regulatory Compliance
location_raw: Richmond, VA; Irving, TX; Overland Park, KS
description:
The Director, Regulatory Compliance will establish and lead a scalable enterprise program for emerging electric-reliability obligations affecting large computational loads and company-owned high-voltage infrastructure. This leader will translate evolving regulatory requirements into clear governance, accountable controls, auditable evidence, and practical operating requirements across the asset lifecycle. The role combines NERC compliance leadership, reliability assurance, executive risk communication, regulatory engagement, and cross-functional program execution. This role represents organizational groups to interface with NERC, FERC, Regional Entities, RTOs/ISOs, utilities and industry groups.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Develop and execute the long-term regulatory compliance and reliability assurance strategy for QTS utility operations.

- Lead enterprise applicability reviews, registration strategy, new-entity registration activities, and implementation planning for applicable NERC Reliability Standards and related requirements.

- Provide executive-level assessments of compliance posture, emerging obligations, material risks, resource needs, and mitigation priorities.

- Monitor, interpret, and communicate developments from NERC, FERC, Regional Entities, RTOs/ISOs, utilities, reliability coordinators, and transmission providers.

- Lead impact assessments for new or revised standards and convert technical requirements into actionable plans for affected business functions and assets.

- Coordinate regulatory positions and external communications with Legal, Risk, technical subject matter experts, outside counsel, and consultants.

- Design and maintain a risk-based Internal Controls Program that embeds compliance requirements into design, commissioning, operations, maintenance, protection, monitoring, and change-management processes.

- Direct development and maintenance of NERC Compliance Procedures, Reliability Standard Audit Worksheets, evidence requirements, retention rules, and auditable data repositories.

- Build continuous audit readiness through self-assessments, mock audits, evidence quality reviews, issue tracking, corrective actions, mitigation plans, and lessons learned.

- Lead organizational responses to audits, inquiries, investigations, self-reports, enforcement matters, and remediation activities when applicable.

- Integrate requirements with Utility Engineering, Utility Asset Management, Development, Facilities Operations, cybersecurity, enterprise technology, Legal/Risk, and Internal Audit through clear ownership and repeatable workflows.

- Develop scalable internal capability while managing specialist consultants, outside counsel, scopes of work, budgets, deliverables, and knowledge transfer.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in engineering, power systems, business, information systems, cybersecurity, risk, or a related field, or equivalent directly relevant experience.

- Minimum ten years of progressive experience in electric utility operations, transmission, system operations, reliability compliance, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity compliance, risk, or a related highly regulated environment.

- At least 5 years of leadership experience managing complex compliance, reliability, operational, risk, or governance programs and teams.

- Demonstrated knowledge of the NERC regulatory framework and applicable Operations & Planning and/or Critical Infrastructure Protection Reliability Standards.

- Experience building or materially improving compliance governance, internal controls, evidence programs, policies, procedures, corrective-action processes, and audit readiness.

- Experience leading or supporting regulatory audits, compliance assessments, investigations, remediation, mitigation, self-certification, or enforcement-response activities.

- Proven ability to analyze complex technical and regulatory requirements, assess enterprise impact and risk, and communicate decisions and recommendations to executive and technical audiences.

- Able to travel up to 30% of the time or as needed to support relationship building and delivery.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Fifteen or more years leading in NERC-related projects

- Direct experience with a NERC-registered entity, Regional Entity, utility, ISO/RTO, independent power producer, large-load customer, or critical-infrastructure operator.

- Experience with entity registration, Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program activities, standards development, regulatory committees, or industry working groups.

- Working knowledge of power-system modeling, transmission planning, protection and control, disturbance monitoring, operational communications, voltage/frequency ride-through, large-load interconnection, or system operations.

- Experience implementing GRC or compliance-management technology, structured evidence repositories, workflow automation, and compliance dashboards.

- Experience establishing a compliance organization or scaling a program across multiple regions and assets.

- Professional certification such as CCEP, CISA, CRISC, CISSP, or a relevant NERC credential; advanced degree in a related discipline.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

- Ability to travel and participate as needed for regulatory meetings, audits, site engagement, stakeholder forums, and industry events.

title: Director, Event Strategy & Operations
location_raw: US KS Overland Park; Ashburn, VA; Atlanta, GA
description:
The Director, Event Strategy & Operations will lead the company-wide events function for QTS, including executive-level meetings, customer and partner events, internal leadership events, industry engagements, tradeshows, site activations, and other high-visibility brand moments. This role is responsible for shaping event strategy, bringing forward fresh ideas, and translating business priorities into events that are thoughtful, well-run, and aligned to QTS goals.

This leader must be able to think strategically while also operating as a doer. They will own planning, logistics, run of show, vendor coordination, budget management, executive stakeholder communication, onsite execution, and post-event reporting. The role requires strong executive presence, high professionalism, sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to build trusted relationships across the company.

What You Will Do:

Event Strategy and Creative Leadership

- Lead the event strategy for QTS-hosted and attended events, ensuring each event has a clear purpose, audience, business objective, and desired outcome.

- Bring forward creative, executive-ready event concepts that elevate QTS, support the brand, and create stronger engagement with customers, partners, employees, and communities.

- Serve as the events thought partner to Brand, Marketing, Communications, Sales, External Affairs, and senior leadership teams.

- Identify new approaches, industry trends, and experience opportunities that help QTS show up with more polish, consistency, and impact.

Executive and C-Level Event Ownership

- Own planning and execution for high-profile, C-level, CEO, customer, partner, and board-facing events, including executive briefing needs, guest experience, run of show, and onsite readiness.

- Interact directly with executives and senior stakeholders with confidence, clarity, professionalism, and appropriate urgency.

- Anticipate executive needs, risks, sensitivities, and decision points before they become issues.

- Ensure events reflect the right tone, level of quality, and business importance for the audience.

Operational Execution and Team Leadership

- Lead the centralized event planning team and establish clear swim lanes, priorities, timelines, and standards for execution.

- Administer all phases of the event process, including planning, logistics, registration, staffing, catering, transportation, audiovisual, signage, collateral, run of show, onsite execution, teardown, and post-event follow-up.

- Operate as a hands-on leader who can both direct the work and step in to execute when needed.

- Build strong team routines, including planning meetings, status updates, check-ins, decision logs, and issue escalation paths.

- Coach, develop, and hold team members accountable for quality, professionalism, responsiveness, and follow-through.

Process, Reporting, and Measurement

- Build repeatable pre-event and post-event processes that create consistency across event types and reduce last-minute fire drills.

- Develop event intake, planning, reporting, and prioritization tools that help the organization understand workload, goals, outcomes, and resource needs.

- Create an event ROI and impact model appropriate to the event type, including attendance, engagement, stakeholder feedback, budget performance, and business outcomes where available.

- Use post-event learnings to improve future planning, vendor decisions, team resourcing, and executive reporting.

Budget, Vendor, and Risk Management

- Manage event budgets, vendor relationships, contracts, negotiations, timelines, and invoice reconciliation in alignment with QTS policies and processes.

- Partner with procurement, legal, accounting , security, facilities, and other teams as needed to support compliant event execution.

- Identify risks and dependencies early, provide clear recommendations, and manage tradeoffs without losing momentum.

- Ensure all events are delivered with strong attention to detail, cost discipline, and operational readiness.

What You Will Need to be Successful:

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

- 10+ years of experience leading large-scale corporate events, executive meetings, customer or partner events, conferences, tradeshows, site activations, or similar high-visibility events.

- 5+ years of people leadership experience directly supervising an event planning function or event team.

- Demonstrated experience owning executive-level or C-level events from strategy through onsite execution and post-event follow-up.

- Experience managing event budgets, vendor negotiations, contracts, timelines, logistics, and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Ability to travel and work outside standard business hours as needed, approximately 40% travel.

Nice To Have:

- 10+ years of management experience directly supervising an event planning function and team.

- Experience supporting events in a fast-paced, high-growth, B2B, technology, infrastructure, real estate, data center, or similar business environment.

- Experience with executive briefing, customer experience, partner engagement, community/site activation, or board-level event support.

- Experience building event processes, intake models, calendars, reporting dashboards, ROI frameworks, or event playbooks.

- Experience overseeing branded merchandise, fulfillment vendors, executive gifting, or promotional inventory programs.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

- High level of professionalism, executive presence, tact, diplomacy, discretion, and judgment in sensitive or confidential matters.

- Creative and innovative thinker who can bring new ideas while staying practical about budget, timing, resources, and execution.

- Strong operator who is organized, detail-oriented, decisive, and able to manage multiple demands and changing priorities.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief executives and align stakeholders quickly.

- Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with the ability to build productive relationships across all levels of the organization.

- Strong team leadership, coaching, performance management, and delegation skills.

- Advanced project management skills, including timeline management, dependency tracking, issue resolution, and risk mitigation.

- Ability to apply analytical and problem-solving skills to event planning, team workload, budget, and post-event measurement.

- Commitment to customer service for internal and external audiences.

- Ability to operate under pressure, deadlines, and the demands of a busy office environment.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and related presentation, database, and spreadsheet applications .

title: QTS Commissioning Team
location_raw: Glendale, AZ; Eagle Mountain, UT; York, SC; Denver, CO; Cedar Rapids, IA; Fayetteville, GA
description:

This role will be a platform role that may require an estimated 75% travel to other sites around the U.S.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Assist in all site construction activity and installations, in coordination with QTS Development Team, external construction resources, to ensure system design, installation and testing adhere to operational standards.

- Develop comprehensive commissioning plans for Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, and Level 5 systems, including connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, Electrical, Mechanical, and Building Automation components.

- Conduct thorough commissioning activities, ensuring that all systems are installed, tested, and validated according to industry standards and client specifications.

- Identify, track, and resolve any issues during the commissioning process, working closely with the project team to resolve technical challenges.  Utilize findings and provide feedback to program management team to drive continuous improvement.

- Create and/or review detailed commissioning documentation, including test procedures, reports, and as-built documentation, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

- Witness testing of all equipment during commissioning and validate sequence of operations and receipt of all operational documentation.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design engineers, project managers, contractors, commissioning agents, and facilities operations to ensure seamless integration of systems during the commissioning phase without impact to operational portions of the campus or building.

- Implement quality control measures to ensure the highest standards are met during the build and commissioning process, adhering to regulatory requirements and industry best practices.

- Develop and test site specific standard operating procedures (SOP), method of procedures (MOP), and emergency response procedures (ERP) in coordination with facilities operations.

- Provide training to end-users and maintenance personnel on the operation and maintenance of commissioned systems.

- Uses the Change Management Process to get approval for preventative and corrective maintenance.  Commences & completes the maintenance along with the necessary documentation using the QTS process and software.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Project Management, Computer Science, or a related field or equivalent professional experience

- Five or more years of work experience in data center engineering, commissioning, project management, or equivalent.

- Background in areas of building maintenance, CCTV and Access control systems, network, telecommunications, and/or fire detection/suppression systems.

- Ability to travel to other Data Center locations as required.

- Proficiency with MS Office Suite.

- US Citizenship for this position is required by law due to federal customer contracts

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Firm understanding of both mechanical and electrical equipment, systems and design related to data centers.

- Knowledge of electricity and medium to low voltage electrical distribution systems

- Experience with emergency backup systems (generators, UPS, battery backup)

- Knowledge of equipment operation and maintenance, single line drawings, critical scripted work, and sequence of operations.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

- Ability to analyze operations of various systems, determine the cause of problems and malfunctions and take corrective action as required.

- Ability to develop solutions and create technical plans on projects
- Strong written, verbal and interpersonal skills.

title: Principal DCIM Design Engineer
location_raw: Phoenix, AZ; US TX Remote; US UT Remote
description:
The Principal DCIM Design Engineer is responsible for the design, standardization, coordination, and delivery of advanced building management and power monitoring systems (BMS, EPMS, SCADA) across the QTS data center portfolio. This role serves as a design and standards leader, partner integrator, and systems strategist for scalable delivery of Data Center Infrastructure Management platforms. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in industrial controls engineering, coupled with strategic design experience in mission-critical environments. They will drive development of design standards, sequence of operations, instrumentation and control documentation, alarming strategies, integration models, and commissioning readiness across our portfolio. The candidate must demonstrate strong vendor coordination, mentoring capability, and an aptitude for cross-functional leadership.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES - Other duties may be assigned. –

- Lead development and refinement of the DCIM design Basis of Design (BOD) and owner requirements.

- Manage, onboard, and lead AEOR Controls teams as well as owner directed Design System Integrator (DSI) to include business review and cadenced calibrations.

- Direct design consultants and partners in defining architecture, instrumentation, alarming and integration requirements for control systems.

- Develop and implement enterprise-wide controls and alarming standards across BMS/EPMS/SCADA platforms.

- Define product and platform requirements across Aveva System Platform, Ignition, and open I/O frameworks.

- Lead internal reviews of sequence of operations, system architecture, and P&ID diagrams.

- Champion point naming conventions, alarming logic, historical data trending structure, and DCIM integration schemas.

- Collaborate with consultants and integrators during software and factory testing, and ensure consistency with QTS expectations.

- Provide QA/QC oversight during design, deployment, and commissioning.

- Drive digital twin and simulation initiatives to de-risk controls logic and optimize system behavior pre-deployment.

- Partner with procurement and project teams to support Scope of Work (SOW) creation, RFP responses, and vendor onboarding.

title: Cost Control Manager
location_raw: Chicago, IL
description:
The Cost Control Manager is responsible for managing construction budgets from project inception through completion in accordance with the construction contract documents including validation of potential change orders and associated cost. This position involves leading and collaborating with various stakeholders, including project management teams (internal and external), vendors, cost consultants, and finance and accounting teams. The ideal candidate has strong collaboration skills, advanced knowledge of construction documents, analytical abilities, attention to detail, and proficiency in financial and project management software tools.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

- Examine construction contract documents and ensure continuous compliance with the contract and relevant laws.

- Evaluate contractors' requests to award (RTA) to subcontractors, provide recommendations to the project management team for review, and monitor buyout savings.

- During the monthly review of the pay application, ensure that contractors' schedule of values aligns with the contract, verify the required monthly documentation, reconcile the project budget as needed, and inform the project management teams.

- Initiate purchase orders for vendors and ensure invoices comply with the agreed terms.

- Obtain detailed monthly cash flow projections from the contractor, reconcile projections with actual figures, and provide these projections to the capital and investment teams.

- Evaluate potential change order events by thoroughly reviewing contract documents and relevant cost information and offer well-informed recommendations to project management teams including substantiating claim positions.

- Maintain a log of potential change orders and their approximate costs, track approved change orders, manage the internal approval process for change orders according to the delegation of authority, and ensure review by the legal department as necessary.

- Support the finance team with the monthly loan draw process as required, including acquiring any necessary documentation from the contractor or its subcontractors.

- Conduct weekly and biweekly meetings with external construction managers, internal project management teams, and consultants to review pay applications, required documentation, and change order status. Ensure that all teams adhere to the specified review timelines.

- Manage third party change management or cost auditing teams that are assigned to the project.

- Advanced knowledge in construction contract documents and change management.

- Proficiency in financial and project management software (e.g., Workday, e-Builder, Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud).

- Ability to work within dynamic and diverse team and environment.

- Ability to lead and mentor others.

- Ability to travel up to 75% of the time

- Seven or more years of experience in construction or project management.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Ten or more years of experience in construction or project management preferred.

title: Sr. Water Quality Engineer
location_raw: Cedar Rapids, IA; Eagle Mountain, UT; York, SC; Phoenix, AZ
description:
Senior Water Quality Engineer
Position Summary
The Senior Water Quality Engineer is responsible for providing technical leadership for water quality programs that support the design, construction, commissioning, and operation of mission-critical data center infrastructure. This role focuses on optimizing water quality and treatment for cooling systems, chilled water plants, cooling towers, reclaimed water systems, and other mechanical infrastructure to maximize reliability, efficiency, and sustainability.
Working closely with engineering, EHS, operations, and sustainability teams, the Senior Water Quality Engineer develops water management strategies, establishes technical standards, evaluates emerging technologies, and supports portfolio projects from concept through operations.

This role requires work hours to support a 7X24X365 data center environment.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned.

- Lead the development and implementation of water quality strategies for hyperscale and enterprise data center campuses.

- Establish engineering standards for cooling water chemistry, treatment programs, and system performance.

- Support the design, commissioning, operation, and maintenance of cooling towers, chilled water systems, heat rejection equipment, and associated water infrastructure.

- Evaluate municipal, reclaimed, groundwater, and alternative water sources for data center cooling applications.

- Develop water balance models and optimize facility Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE).

- Collaborate with engineering and sustainability teams to integrate water-efficient cooling solutions into data center designs.

- Analyze water chemistry, corrosion, scaling, microbiological activity, and treatment performance to ensure long-term equipment reliability.

- Develop water management plans that comply with applicable regulations and industry standards, including Legionella risk management.

- Review water treatment vendor performance and recommend improvements to chemical treatment programs.

- Support commissioning activities, startup procedures, and operational readiness for new facilities.

- Investigate water quality incidents, equipment failures, and operational issues, performing root cause analyses and implementing corrective actions.

- Evaluate innovative cooling technologies, including liquid cooling, closed-loop systems, reclaimed water reuse, and alternative cooling strategies.

- Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership across multidisciplinary project teams.

- Support global infrastructure expansion by providing subject matter expertise on water quality and water stewardship initiatives.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

- Bachelor's of Science degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Environmental Engineering, OR equivalent professional experience in lieu of degree

- Minimum of seven years of experience in industrial water treatment, water quality engineering, cooling water systems, or mission-critical infrastructure.

- Strong knowledge of cooling water chemistry, corrosion control, scaling prevention, microbiological control, and chemical treatment programs.

- Experience with cooling towers, chilled water plants, condenser water systems, and industrial water treatment.

- Experience managing complex engineering projects across multiple stakeholders.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret water quality data and operational trends.

- Excellent communication, technical writing, and presentation skills.

- Ability to travel (up to 50%) to other Data Center locations as required.

Preferred Qualifications

- Ten or more years of experience in industrial water treatment, water quality engineering, cooling water systems, or mission-critical infrastructure, four or more years of which were conducted in hyperscale or enterprise data centers.

- Knowledge of liquid cooling technologies for high-density computing environments.

- Experience with ASHRAE guidance related to data center cooling and water systems.

- Familiarity with water sustainability strategies, water reuse, and alternative water sourcing.

- Experience supporting commissioning and startup of mission-critical facilities.

- Knowledge of environmental permitting, industrial wastewater management, and stormwater compliance.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

- Advanced knowledge of industrial water treatment and cooling water systems.

- Strong understanding of corrosion science, scaling mechanisms, microbiological control, and water chemistry.

- Knowledge of water efficiency metrics, including Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE).

- Familiarity with CFD-informed cooling strategies and heat rejection systems is desirable.

- Ability to develop engineering standards and best practices for global infrastructure.

- Strong project management and organizational skills.

- Ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary engineering teams.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office, AutoCAD, Bluebeam, BIM collaboration platforms, and water chemistry modeling and data analysis tools.

Working Conditions

- Combination of office, laboratory, and field work.

- Periodic travel (up to 40%) to domestic and international data center sites.

- Site visits may include active construction environments, operating mission-critical facilities, and industrial mechanical plants.

- Occasional after-hours support during commissioning activities or critical operational events.

Core Competencies

- Mission-Critical Infrastructure

- Water Quality Engineering

- Industrial Water Treatment

- Cooling Systems Optimization

- Sustainability & Water Stewardship

- Engineering Standards Development

- Root Cause Analysis

- Project Leadership

- Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Continuous Improvement

title: Technology Product Lead - Supply Chain
location_raw: Suwanee, GA; Ashburn, VA; Irving, TX; Overland Park, KS
description:
Technology Product Lead

Why This Role Exists

We are building a Product organization to bring  clear ownership, prioritization, and outcome accountability  to critical technology platforms that power our business.

Today, much of our platform and systems engineering work is executed through strong teams and capable technology, but without consistent  end-to-end ownership of outcomes , clear  value identification , or transparent  measurement of impact . Important work gets delivered, but it’s often difficult to answer fundamental questions:

- Why is this the right work , r ight now?

- What outcomes are we driving?

- How do we know it’s working?

The  Product Lead  role exists to close that gap.

This role is aligned to our   Asset Management value stream , with a focus on shaping the technology capabilities that enable end-to-end visibility, control, and optimization of assets and materials across their lifecycle. The Product Lead operates at the intersection of supply chain operations and enterprise technology, partnering with procurement, logistics, construction, and operations teams to turn complex, often undefined asset-related challenges into clear product direction and outcome-oriented capabilities.

This includes defining and evolving capabilities that support asset lifecycle tracking, materials planning and forecasting, inventory and warehouse management, supplier coordination, and asset performance and utilization. The Product Lead takes a   multi-platform approach   and supports and shepherds solutions across ERP, asset management, supply chain, and logistics systems, ensuring that capability design is driven by the problem to solve rather than constrained by existing tools.

The role emphasizes   deep engagement in discovery, ideation, and rapid iteration , identifying opportunities, challenging assumptions, and shaping solutions in close partnership with both business and technology teams. Rather than coordinating delivery, the Product Lead is expected to   drive clarity where none exists , framing the “why,” establishing clear scope boundaries, and prioritizing work to enable incremental value delivery through iterative execution led by architecture and delivery partners.

Success in this role depends on the ability to connect fragmented systems and data into cohesive, actionable capabilities that improve transparency, reduce operational friction, and accelerate decision-making across the asset lifecycle, from sourcing and delivery through deployment, maintenance, and optimization. This role is best suited for individuals   who are energized by   building in ambiguity, shaping new capabilities, and creating structure from complex, evolving environments.

How We Think About Product Ownership

We view product ownership as a  continuous spectrum , not a fixed state:

- NOW : Capability-based ownership and platform stabilization

- NEXT : Value-aligned recomposition and shared accountability

- LATER : True end-to-end value streams with economic ownership

Importantly:

The work does not change.
Only how we frame ownership, outcomes, and success evolves.

Product Leads are expected to operate comfortably across this spectrum ,   protecting near-term execution while intentionally shaping longer-term outcome ownership.

What You’ll Own

Product Leads are anchored to one or more  capability-aligned product areas , such as:

- Core   T ransaction   P latforms

- Commercial   E nablement

- Enterprise   D ata &   I ntelligence

- Developer &   P latform   E nablement

- Trust, risk, and compliance

While each Product Lead is assigned to a specific area, the scope is intentionally designed to evolve from platform stewardship toward outcome and value-driven ownership over time.

Role Mandate

As a Product Lead, you are accountable for:

- Defining  what should be built and why

- Making  priority and scope tradeoffs  within defined investment guardrails

- Owning  product outcomes , not just delivery

- Ensuring clarity and continuity from strategy through execution

This role blends  strategic thinking with hands-on product work . Product Leads are expected to move fluidly between defining outcomes, shaping work, and partnering with delivery teams to ensure intent is clearly understood and executed.

What You’ll Do

Product Vision, Strategy & Outcomes

- Shape and evolve product vision and roadmaps aligned to organizational goals and technology strategy

- Translate business objectives into clear product outcomes, hypotheses, and success measures

- Align platform capabilities to   KPI oriented   outcomes such as scalability, reliability, automation, efficiency, and risk reduction

- Advocate for investments that measurably improve productivity and operational effectiveness

- Balance short-term delivery needs with long-term strategic outcomes

Hands-On Product Ownership & Execution

- Own product backlogs end-to-end, ensuring work is clearly defined, sequenced, and aligned to outcomes

- Write and refine epics, features, and user stories as needed ;   especially for complex, high-impact, or ambiguous work

- Lead backlog building and ongoing refinement to maintain a healthy, outcome-oriented pipeline of work

- Partner closely with engineering and architecture to shape solutions, identify dependencies, and surface risks early

- Validate usefulness and impact of delivered capabilities with internal users and stakeholders

Leadership, Decision-Making & Collaboration

- Serve as the primary decision-maker for prioritization, sequencing, and scope within your product area

- Foster collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across cross-functional teams

- Empower teams with clarity of intent while allowing flexibility in how work is delivered

- Make informed decisions under ambiguity, time pressure, or incomplete information

- Actively remove obstacles to progress and value delivery

Ceremonies, Cadence & Flow

- Lead or actively participate in key product-focused ceremonies, including backlog refinement and product planning

- Ensure shared understanding of priorities, intent, and success criteria across teams

- Partner with delivery leaders to support agile ways of working without becoming process-bound

- Adjust focus and level of involvement as products, teams, and maturity evolve

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

- Act as the primary liaison between engineering, architecture, business partners, and leadership

- Communicate priorities, progress, tradeoffs, and outcomes clearly and consistently

- Maintain transparency to build trust and alignment across teams and departments

- Continuously gather feedback and pain points to inform roadmap and backlog decisions

Metrics, Learning & Value Realization

- Define and track KPIs tied to efficiency, performance, reliability, and business impact

- Use data and analytics to inform prioritization and validate hypotheses

- Monitor adoption and outcomes of delivered capabilities

- Translate results and learning into roadmap and backlog adjustments

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- 8+ years of experience in   technical product management , technical product leadership, or related roles

- Demonstrated ability to own outcomes  and  operate hands-on at the delivery level

- Experience writing epics, features, and user stories in complex technical environments

- Proven ability to make prioritization and scope tradeoffs aligned to business value

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven mindset

- Experience partnering closely with engineering, architecture, and operations teams

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and influencing without formal authority

- Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- Background in   platform engineering ,   infrastructure ,   DevOps , SRE, or   enterprise systems

- Experience in organizations transitioning from project-centric to product-centric models

- Familiarity with agile and   lean product practices   in enterprise environments

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

- Relationships – Build valuable relationships with people, facts and context.  Unlock the power of people to overcome challenges to achieve more.

- Creativity – Apply integrated thinking to produce unprecedented value.  Combine new facts and deeper understanding people’s purpose and concerns to generate a surplus of ideas.

- Collaboration – Develop aggressive yet realistic plans.  Work collaboratively to make the best decision on allocation of time, resources and talent.

- Accountability – Get the job done.  Be clear on who is going to do what and when.

- Learning – Lead in a developmental environment.  Turn learning into action.  Embrace change and appreciate others.

- Transformational leader with the heart of serving others.

TOTAL REWARDS

- This role is also eligible for a competitive beneﬁts package that includes: medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; ﬂexible spending and HSA accounts; paid holidays; paid time off; paid volunteer days; employee assistance program; tuition assistance; parental leave; military leave assistance; QTS scholarship for dependents; wellness program, and other company beneﬁts.

- This position is bonus eligible.
